input_references.role: Vessel type and continuous dimensions linked by vessel_id

metadata.goal: Analyze how vessel traffic and movement patterns vary across different periods of the day.
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed Danish AIS-style North Sea case containing 88 complete trajectories grouped by departure period across early morning, midday, late afternoon, and evening/night, with static vessel dimensions and type.
metadata.source_note: The geographic setting is west of Jutland; visible trajectories and temporal relationships are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: In the early morning and later afternoon, traffic contains more small-vessel movements and more frequent short-term COG changes than during comparable evening and midday periods.

plot.title: Small-vessel Activity and COG Changes
plot.description: Temporal distributions expose the stated time-of-day movement difference.

insight_list.question: How do the length-and-width vessel-size composition and short-term COG changes vary across time periods?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Classify a vessel as small only when both length is below 70 m and width is below 15 m, assign trajectories by departure period, then compare the hourly rate of COG changes exceeding 5 degrees between adjacent reports no more than 7 minutes apart.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path).sort_values(['trajectory_id','point_index']); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path); points['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(points.timestamp)
delta=points.groupby('trajectory_id').cog.diff(); interval=points.groupby('trajectory_id').timestamp.diff().dt.total_seconds()/60; points['short_cog_change']=(abs((delta+180)%360-180)>5)&(interval<=7)
trips=points.groupby('trajectory_id').agg(vessel_id=('vessel_id','first'),start=('timestamp','min'),end=('timestamp','max'),short_cog_changes=('short_cog_change','sum')).reset_index().merge(vessels,on='vessel_id'); trips['duration_hours']=(trips.end-trips.start).dt.total_seconds()/3600; trips['short_cog_change_rate_per_hour']=trips.short_cog_changes/trips.duration_hours
hour=trips.start.dt.hour; trips['period']=np.select([(hour>=4)&(hour<9),(hour>=9)&(hour<14),(hour>=14)&(hour<19)],['early_morning','midday','late_afternoon'],default='evening_night'); trips['small_vessel']=(trips.length_m<70)&(trips.width_m<15)
summary=trips.groupby('period').agg(trajectories=('trajectory_id','size'),small_vessels=('small_vessel','sum'),mean_event_rate_per_hour=('short_cog_change_rate_per_hour','mean'),median_event_rate_per_hour=('short_cog_change_rate_per_hour','median')); print(summary.round(2).to_string())

insight_list.question: How do vessel speed level and stability vary across the four time periods, and is late-afternoon variability especially strong for fishing vessels?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare trajectory mean SOG and within-trajectory SOG variability by departure period, separating fishing from other vessels when assessing variability.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path); points['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(points.timestamp)
trips=points.groupby('trajectory_id').agg(vessel_id=('vessel_id','first'),start=('timestamp','min'),mean_sog=('sog_knots','mean'),sog_sd=('sog_knots','std')).reset_index().merge(vessels,on='vessel_id')
hour=trips.start.dt.hour; trips['period']=np.select([(hour>=4)&(hour<9),(hour>=9)&(hour<14),(hour>=14)&(hour<19)],['early_morning','midday','late_afternoon'],default='evening_night'); trips['vessel_group']=np.where(trips.ship_type.eq('Fishing'),'fishing','other_vessels')
print(trips.groupby('period').agg(mean_trajectory_sog=('mean_sog','mean'),median_sog_sd=('sog_sd','median'))); print(trips.pivot_table(index='period',columns='vessel_group',values='sog_sd',aggfunc='median'))

insight_list.question: How does heading–COG consistency change in the evening and at night, and how is the gap associated with vessel length and width?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use the circular absolute heading–COG gap, where a smaller value means greater consistency, and relate evening/night-departure gaps to the combined length-by-width footprint.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path); points['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(points.timestamp); points['gap']=abs((points.heading-points.cog+180)%360-180)
trips=points.groupby('trajectory_id').agg(vessel_id=('vessel_id','first'),start=('timestamp','min'),median_gap=('gap','median')).reset_index().merge(vessels,on='vessel_id'); hour=trips.start.dt.hour; night=trips[(hour>=19)|(hour<4)].copy(); night['footprint_m2']=night.length_m*night.width_m; night['small_vessel']=(night.length_m<70)&(night.width_m<15)
print(night.groupby('small_vessel').median_gap.agg(['count','median'])); print(night[['footprint_m2','median_gap']].corr(method='spearman'))

insights: In the early morning and later afternoon, traffic contains more small-vessel movements and more frequent short-term COG changes than during comparable evening and midday periods.
Generally, speeds are stable and higher in the mornings but lower and more variable in the afternoons, especially for fishing vessels.
In the evenings and at night, the consistency between COG and heading decreases, especially for smaller vessels.
summary: In the early morning and later afternoon, traffic contains more small-vessel movements and more frequent short-term COG changes than during comparable evening and midday periods. Generally, speeds are stable and higher in the mornings but lower and more variable in the afternoons, especially for fishing vessels. In the evenings and at night, the consistency between COG and heading decreases, especially for smaller vessels.
